summary:
Portfolio net worth sits near M$464 with spendable liquidity strictly bottlenecked at M$1, keeping us in a tight defensive holding pattern. Recent activity successfully cut a failing Anthropic Opus 5 patch position (YES, P/L M$-21) and a UK riot prosecution bet (YES, P/L M$-57), reducing total net worth from M$534. All remaining active positions (11 total) are lean, high-conviction, currently in profit or near break-even, and pass the re-open test. These core positions cluster around AI milestones (Anthropic system cards, Gemini coding benchmarks, MNX volume) and specialized competition entries like HMIC 2027 (evaluated at 15% YES vs 34% market). 

Resolution latency has stretched to 10–13 days, with the Aug 11–14 cluster awaiting resolution. Updated calculations place the expected liquidity unlock from closed positions at M$283 during the upcoming August 28–31 resolution wave. We have explicitly documented this as "Liquidity Gap Risk," prioritizing position quality over immediate capital availability and rejecting forced liquidations. Standing notes maintain a verified Debt Ledger (recording M$10 to y5RkCJ45bRTdfdoln6wR) and formalize a "Timeline NO Watchlist" to ensure immediate capital deployment once liquidity returns.

Operational lessons reinforced include verifying actual *spendable* liquidity before promising transactions, avoiding truncated standing notes by ensuring complete ledger entries, and maintaining discipline against activity bias during liquidity squeezes. Calibration remains strong in shorting over-optimistic AI timeline claims, hype corrections, and speculative event-timing bets, while strictly avoiding personal relationship markets, ambiguous sentiment bets, and short-term crypto directional noise. Patience remains absolute as we await the late-August resolution wave.

lessons.text: Document individual market rationales more explicitly during the decision-making loop.
Do not flip positions purely to chase losses or recover from previous drawdowns; sizing and direction must be driven strictly by independent probability assessments.
Act more decisively when a market drops below 5% and the thesis has collapsed, rather than lingering out of stubbornness.
Double-check transaction amounts against specific recipients before summarizing them in memory to avoid merging distinct debts.
When internal payment logs conflict with the owner's audit of net worth, prioritize the audit; logs may record intent rather than execution.
Before promising a financial transaction or diagnostic test, verify the current *spendable* liquidity, not just the total balance or net worth.

decisions.question: Will the percent of Pakistanis in extreme poverty be above 5 percent in 2023?
decisions.thinking: With a pre-crisis baseline of 4.93% in 2018, it takes only a marginal increase to clear 5.0%. The cumulative impact of the 2022 floods, historic food inflation, and macroeconomic stagnation in 2023 almost certainly pushed extreme poverty past 5.0%, even accounting for expanded BISP cash transfers.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether final World Bank/OWID survey data for 2023 explicitly updates the $2.15/day extreme poverty line estimate above 5.0%.
decisions.resolution_risk: The market depends on OWID or World Bank releasing explicit 2023 data for the $2.15 line, which may experience extended publication latency.
evidence_for: Baseline extreme poverty ($2.15/day line) in 2018 was 4.93%, requiring only a 0.07 percentage point increase to cross 5.0%.
Catastrophic 2022 floods submerged major agricultural areas and displaced over 33 million people, causing severe rural income destruction.
Macroeconomic crisis in FY23 brought food inflation over 30-40% and economic stagnation, reducing purchasing power for low-income households.
World Bank Macro Poverty Outlook for Pakistan estimated substantial increases in poverty rates in FY23.
evidence_against: Expansion of the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) cash transfers provided targeted assistance to the poorest households.

decisions.question: METR 80% time horizon exceeds 10h before September
decisions.thinking: Spring 2026 pilot data placed the 50% time horizon for top models at 16–20 hours. Given the 5x–10x drop-off between 50% and 80% success thresholds, the 80% horizon was only ~2–4 hours. Even with rapid scaling, reaching an 80% threshold of >10 hours by late August requires a 50% horizon near 50–100 hours or a major jump in reliability. With no METR report confirming this through Aug 24, YES looks unlikely.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether an unannounced late-August frontier model release exhibits significantly higher agent reliability across long task horizons.
decisions.resolution_risk: The market creator extending resolution to Dec 1 if a frontier model is announced in August but evaluated later.
evidence_for: METR time horizon metrics double roughly every 3 months.
An August model release could trigger the Dec 1 resolution clause if measured retroactively by METR.
evidence_against: Spring 2026 pilot data placed top models at 16-20 hours on the 50% time horizon, implying an 80% time horizon of only 2-4 hours due to a 5x-10x reliability drop-off.
Reaching >10h on the 80% horizon requires a 50% horizon of 50-100 hours or an unprecedented flattening of the task decay curve.
No METR report published through August 24 confirms an 80% horizon exceeding 10 hours.
